exercises.title: Similar or opposite meaning? (Ex. 1–2)
exercises.instruction: Do the two underlined words in each sentence have a similar meaning or the opposite meaning?

stimulus.text:
Our friends and protectors

**A** When asked their favourite animals, many people answer 'dolphins'. They are known as friendly, intelligent creatures that have a special relationship with humans. For example, dolphins can tell when a woman is pregnant. They can also tell when someone is in trouble. No one is really sure why this is the case. Experts think they may understand that humans are similar to them and try to protect them from predators and other dangers. Dolphins' protection of humans might not be just automatic or instinctive: they may actively decide to help in certain situations.

**B** There are many stories about dolphins protecting humans from sharks. Wildlife filmmaker Hardy Jones was filming a group of dolphins, when a large shark swam towards him ready to attack. Four dolphins came to his rescue and drove the shark away. Perhaps they could tell he was a person who cared very much about dolphins. In fact, Jones was a well-known campaigner against the killing of dolphins. In another incident, in 2004, in New Zealand, four people were saved from a great white shark by a pod of dolphins. The dolphins herded the swimmers into a group and formed a protective ring around them. As they had not yet seen the shark, one of them tried to swim away. He couldn't get away, because every time he tried, he was pushed back inside the ring by the dolphins.

**C** Dolphins don't only save humans from sharks, but protect them in other situations too. A scuba diver was hit by a boat near the Channel Islands (between England and France) in 2006. The man was unconscious, but survived 56 hours in the water, watched over by a pod of about 150 dolphins. In 2014, dolphins again came to the help of a human. Joey Trevino was losing hope. He had been in the sea for 24 hours after his boat sank in the Gulf of Mexico. He felt he couldn't keep going any more. A friendly dolphin approached him and gently pushed him, as if to say 'don't give up'. That moral support and encouragement may have saved Trevino's life.

**D** Dolphins have also been known to help other species. In New Zealand, two pygmy sperm whales were in difficulty next to a sand bank. People were trying their best to get them back out to sea, but the whales couldn't find their way past the sand bank. After several hours of failed attempts, they were ready to give up. Along came 'Moko', a bottlenose dolphin, who seemed to communicate with the whales and led them to a channel which took them back to the ocean.

**E** Whales have also been known to protect both humans and other mammals. In California, in 2012, a BBC Planet Earth film crew filmed a group of humpback whales who were protecting migrating grey whales from attacks by orcas (killer whales) over a period of at least seven hours. In China, Yang Yun applied for a job training whales at Polar Land in the city of Harbin. For the 'interview' she had to dive down as far as possible in the seven-metre deep pool. When she was about five metres down, Yang Yun found she couldn't move her legs due to the freezing temperatures. Two beluga whales, Mila and Nicola, sensed that she was in trouble. Mila gripped Yang Yun's leg in her mouth and pushed Yun to the surface, saving her life.

**F** Stories of marine mammals helping humans – and each other – date back to Ancient Greece. Although we may never be sure why they help us, many people feel that it is a good reason for us to do whatever we can to protect them.
stimulus.caption: Our friends and protectors (p. 150)

items.prompt: A PREDATOR catches and eats its PREY.
items.explanation: predator = thú săn mồi; prey = con mồi.

items.prompt: A GROUP of dolphins is called a POD.
items.explanation: pod = đàn cá heo, tức là một group → nghĩa giống nhau.

items.prompt: Environmentalists work for the CONSERVATION and PROTECTION of the planet.
items.explanation: conservation (bảo tồn) ≈ protection (bảo vệ) → giống nhau.

items.prompt: Only a few baby turtles SURVIVED; all the others DIED.
items.explanation: survived (sống sót) ↔ died (chết) → trái nghĩa.

items.prompt: Mothers have an AUTOMATIC desire to protect their babies; keeping them safe is INSTINCTIVE behaviour.
items.explanation: automatic (tự động) ≈ instinctive (theo bản năng) → giống nhau.

exercises.title: Words with similar meanings (Ex. 4)
exercises.instruction: Read paragraph B in detail. Then match the words and phrases 1–5 from paragraph B with words and phrases a–e which have similar meanings.

items.explanation: filming ≈ videoing (quay phim).
came to his rescue ≈ saved the life of (cứu sống).
well-known ≈ famous (nổi tiếng).
against the killing of ≈ for the protection of (chống giết hại = bảo vệ).
pod = group of dolphins (đàn cá heo).

exercises.title: Which paragraph? (Ex. 5–7)
exercises.instruction: Answer the questions about where to find the information.

items.prompt: Which paragraph did you need to read in detail to complete the notes about Hardy Jones?
items.explanation: Không cần đọc cả đoạn — chỉ phần về Hardy Jones.

items.prompt: Which paragraph did you need to read to complete the notes about the orcas and the beluga whales?
items.explanation: Thông tin về cá voi sát thủ (orcas) và cá voi trắng (beluga) nằm ở đoạn E.

items.prompt: Which paragraph do you need to read to find the ending to the sentence 'Moko "spoke" to the beached whales …'?
items.explanation: Câu chuyện chú cá heo Moko dẫn đường cho cá voi mắc cạn nằm ở đoạn C.

exercises.title: Choose the ending (Ex. 8–9)
exercises.instruction: Choose one of these endings for the sentence.

items.prompt: Moko 'spoke' to the beached whales …

options.text: because her first attempts had failed.
to help them return to the deep water.
because she led them to safety.

items.explanation: "led them to a channel which took them back to the ocean" = help them return to the deep water. A: attempts/failed là của con người. C: dẫn tới nơi an toàn không phải LÝ DO Moko "nói chuyện" với cá voi.

exercises.title: Possibility or ability? (Ex. 11–12)
exercises.instruction: Find examples of modals in paragraphs A, B, E and F. Is each modal about possibility or ability?

items.text: Dolphins can tell when a woman is pregnant.
items.explanation: can tell = có khả năng nhận biết → ability.

items.text: Experts think they may understand that humans are similar to them.
items.explanation: may understand = có thể (khả năng xảy ra) → possibility.

items.text: Dolphins' protection of humans might not be just automatic or instinctive.
items.explanation: might not be = có lẽ không phải → possibility.

items.text: They may actively decide to help in certain situations.
items.explanation: may actively decide = có thể → possibility.

items.text: Perhaps they could tell he was a person who cared very much about dolphins.
items.explanation: could tell = đã có khả năng nhận ra → ability (quá khứ).
couldn't get away = không thể thoát ra (quá khứ) → ability.

items.text: Yang Yun found she couldn't move her legs due to the freezing temperatures.
items.explanation: couldn't move her legs = không cử động được → ability.

items.text: Although we may never be sure why they help us…
items.explanation: may never be sure = có thể sẽ không bao giờ chắc → possibility.

exercises.title: Complete with a modal (Ex. 11–12)
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentences with can, could, couldn't, may or might.

items.prompt: Dolphins ____ tell when someone is in trouble. (ability, present)
items.explanation: Khả năng ở hiện tại → can.

items.prompt: Joey Trevino felt he ____ keep going any more. (ability, past, negative)
items.explanation: Khả năng trong quá khứ, phủ định → couldn't.

items.prompt: That moral support ____ have saved Trevino's life. (possibility)
items.explanation: Khả năng xảy ra (đoán) → may/might/could have saved.

items.prompt: The whales ____ find their way past the sand bank. (ability, past, negative)
items.explanation: Quá khứ, không thể tìm được lối qua bãi cát → couldn't.

items.prompt: We ____ never be sure why they help us. (possibility)
items.explanation: Khả năng xảy ra → may/might never be sure.

exercises.title: Headings and questions (Ex. 3)
exercises.instruction: Match the headings 1–5 with the questions a–e.

items.explanation: Country of origin (nguồn gốc) → Nó đến từ đâu?
Dangers (mối nguy) → Nó gặp những đe doạ nào?
Diet (chế độ ăn) → Nó ăn gì?
Habitat (môi trường sống) → Nó sống ở đâu?
Physical description (ngoại hình) → Nó trông thế nào?

exercises.title: Headings and notes (Ex. 4)
exercises.instruction: Look at the notes about the animals. Match each note with a heading.

items.explanation: Đến từ châu Phi → nguồn gốc.

items.left: People are using its land for cows and sheep
items.explanation: Đất bị dùng nuôi bò, cừu → mối nguy.
Chủ yếu ăn cỏ → chế độ ăn.
Sống ở vùng đất ngập nước → môi trường sống.
Có tay dài → ngoại hình.

exercises.title: Signposting words (Ex. 5)
exercises.instruction: Look at the signposting phrases. What do they signal?

items.prompt: So, now I'm going to talk a little about …

options.text: a new topic – might be a new heading on the notes
the same thing in different words

items.explanation: 'now I'm going to talk about' → chuyển sang chủ đề mới (thường là đề mục mới trong ghi chú).

items.prompt: Let's have a look at two reasons why …

options.text: a new topic – the last one
two reasons – listen carefully for both
the same thing in different words

items.explanation: 'two reasons why' → báo trước có hai lý do, nghe đủ cả hai.

items.prompt: So, I'll move on to talk about …

options.text: a new topic – might be a new heading on the notes
the first and the second reason

items.explanation: 'move on to' → chuyển chủ đề mới.

items.prompt: Firstly … Secondly …

options.text: the same thing in different words
here is the first reason … and here is the second reason

items.explanation: Firstly… Secondly… → lý do thứ nhất, lý do thứ hai.

items.prompt: I'd like to conclude by talking about …

options.text: a new topic – this will be the last thing the speaker talks about
the same thing in different words

items.explanation: 'conclude by' → chủ đề cuối cùng.

items.prompt: In other words …

options.text: the speaker is going to say the same thing using different words

items.explanation: In other words → nói lại cùng ý bằng từ khác.

exercises.title: What kind of word? (Ex. 7)
exercises.instruction: Look at the gaps 1–5 in the notes about the mountain gorilla. What kind of word do you have to listen for?

items.left: Gap 1: Builds a nest on the ___
items.explanation: on the ___ → một nơi chốn (vd. ground).

items.left: Gap 2: Older males have a ___ coloured coat
items.explanation: ___ coloured → một màu sắc.
are called ___ → một tên gọi.

items.left: Gap 4: Plants provide the ___ they require
items.right: something gorillas need to eat or drink
items.explanation: Plants provide the ___ they require → thứ gorilla cần ăn/uống (vd. water).
Dangers: ___ → điều có hại cho gorilla.

exercises.title: Gaps and questions (Ex. 10)
exercises.instruction: Read the notes about the American bullfrog. Match gaps 1–6 in the notes with the questions a–f.

items.left: Gap 1: introduced into the UK at the beginning of the ___ century
items.right: When did it come to Britain?
items.explanation: at the beginning of the ___ century → khi nào tới Anh.

items.left: Gap 2: female weighs up to ___ grams
items.explanation: weighs up to ___ grams → nặng bao nhiêu.

items.right: What part of its body is flat?
items.explanation: has a flat ___ → bộ phận nào dẹt.

items.left: Gap 4: male frog has a ___ coloured throat
items.right: What colour is the throat of the male?
items.explanation: ___ coloured throat → màu cổ họng con đực.

items.left: Gap 5: eats … birds and animals including ___
items.right: What kind of animals does it eat?
items.explanation: eats … including ___ → ăn loài vật nào.

items.left: Gap 6: a total of £___ already spent
items.right: How much money has been spent on control measures?
items.explanation: £___ spent → đã chi bao nhiêu tiền.
